title: V3B Microtopic Library Package — PROPOSED
description: Structural exchange proposal only. State labels do not authorize acceptance; references, semantics, review authority and curriculum support require separate validation.

schema_version.description: 0.2.0 adds the depth fields the learner quality contract (Shared/quality/learner-quality.v1.json) needs: microtopic.construction_units, question.hint_ladder, representation_roles, independent_check, failure_signal, family_exposure. They are optional in the schema so every package loads; Shared/tools/package_depth.py turns each missing one into a named duty. Migrate with Shared/tools/package_migrate.py.

title.description: Learner-facing unit title; existing packages own this instead of a manifest override.

application_contexts.description: Application/scenario contexts for question families and items. Contexts describe where capabilities are exercised; they are not capabilities, prerequisites, learner-state keys, or mastery targets.

role.description: What the step does to the state. A DECLARE step fixes a convention or a domain and legitimately produces no computation; a TRANSFORM step changes the mathematical state and must show the changed state, not describe it; a VERIFY step checks a result against something already established.

source_ref.description: The source this step's claim rests on. Absent means the step is the author's own construction, which is legitimate and is not the same as source-supported.

reasoning_move.description: One explicit application reasoning move. This is a cognitive state transition (why/which move and its result), not merely a line of arithmetic working.

representation_ref.description: Optional canonical representation that makes this reasoning move visible.

source_ref.description: Optional source binding for a claim carried by this move.

scaffold.description: An authored pedagogical scaffold usable by Core2, Core2A or Core2B. It is deliberately separate from question.hints[], which preserves source/question hint custody; Core2B additionally constrains scaffolds through transfer.protected_move_ref.

text.description: The bounded reveal/support body. For Core2 Prompt/Reveal support this is what becomes visible only after the learner requests the reveal.

prompt.description: Optional Core2 v2 learner prompt shown before the bounded reveal. When present it is paired with learner_stage so stage semantics are explicit rather than inferred from prose.

learner_stage.description: Optional Core2 v2 learner-facing support stage. This classifies the Prompt/Reveal job; it does not change source custody or support_kind. CRUX names the move a learner is most likely to miss, FORMAL_MODEL gives the relation or equation to use, CHECKPOINT gives the intermediate result to compare against.

support_kind.description: What cognitive help the scaffold provides.

reveals.description: How much of the route/result the scaffold discloses.

supports_move_ref.description: Stable id of the reasoning_route move this scaffold supports.

response.description: An honest self-learner's commitment control, not a grading or anti-cheating rule.

reasoning_route.description: Structured application reasoning route. When present with crux_move_ref, this is authoritative for Core2/Core2A/Core2B reasoning semantics; reasoning[] remains the legacy prose fallback.

crux_move_ref.description: Stable id of the question-specific reasoning move that is the primary learner crux. Intake validates that it resolves inside reasoning_route[].

numeric.description: The answer's headline result as a structured candidate, so a subject validator can actually check it. A value stated only inside prose is not machine-checkable, and dropping the check because the value is unstructured would silently discard the oracle.

rubric.description: What a good justification contains, not only what the final result is. answer.kind already has a RUBRIC value; this is where that value points.

difficult_move.description: Legacy index into reasoning[] of the first move a learner is likely to miss. During migration, reasoning_route[] + crux_move_ref are authoritative when present; this index remains the backward-compatible fallback for older records.

extensions.description: Namespaced subject extensions; no scientific authority is inferred.

caption.description: The text printed with a figure in its source, where this resource is a figure. Its title is what the resource is called; its caption is what the source said about it, and custody of an original figure that drops the caption is not custody.

extensions.description: Namespaced subject extensions; no scientific authority is inferred.
Namespaced subject extensions; no scientific authority is inferred.

id.description: Stable identifier, so a teaching step can cite the convention it uses.

statement.description: What is fixed, in the words a learner reads.

conventions.description: Whatever must be fixed before the bucket's quantities can be read. The engine does not enumerate the kinds: an axis convention, a sign convention, a reference state and a phase are all one thing here, and which of them exist is the subject's to say.

scope.description: The bucket's own scope statement. The package carries a scope_summary for the whole package; a learner reading one bucket needs that bucket's.

excluded.description: What is deliberately excluded. An exclusion stated here is a decision; an exclusion nobody wrote down is a gap.

extension_refs.description: What is carried as labelled extension rather than excluded, by extension id.

primary_representation_ref.description: The one figure that orients the whole bucket, for the compact notes. Declared rather than inferred: picking the first representation, or the one with the most instances, would make the map of a bucket depend on authoring order. A bucket with representations and no declared primary is a finding, because the omission is then visible instead of silent.

extensions.description: Namespaced subject extensions; no scientific authority is inferred.

oracle.description: How this exit answer is stood behind. Exactly one of: `verification`, naming a subject validator and binding its inputs to declared data; `held_by`, naming the known issue that explains why no oracle exists yet; or `no_numeric_claim`, saying why the answer asserts no computed value. Silence is not an option, because the exit answer is what a learner measures themselves against.

prerequisite_refs.description: Capability ids this microtopic assumes. A capability of another subject is written '<Subject>:<capability id>' (e.g. 'Mathematics:CAP-MATH-DERIVATIVE-RATE'); package_depth.py emits TEACH_PREREQUISITE_BRIDGE for any ref no library teaches.

elicitation.description: The self-tutor cycle. Four of its six steps live here; diagnose and repair are misconceptions[].wrong_idea, .diagnostic_prompt and .repair, which already hold the same claim for the declarative product. A second home for one truth is the defect the authority gate exists to close.

predict.description: Pose the decision before revealing anything.

prompt.description: The decision, posed so a learner can commit to an answer.

defensible_answer.description: The answer that commitment is judged against. A prompt with no defensible answer is a musing, not a prediction.

attempt.description: What the learner produces, and how it closes without a tutor.

produces.description: What the learner should construct, draw, discriminate or explain.

closure.description: Which form of closure this attempt uses. Each value demands something the others do not, so that none is a synonym an author can pick to avoid work: MODEL_RESPONSE requires model_response, CRITERIA requires rubric, and RUBRIC requires rubric with accepted and rejected examples -- the spec's 'a rubric plus representative accepted and rejected answers', which is the stronger claim of the three.

model_response.description: Closure as one response, where one is right.

rubric.description: Closure as a rubric, where several responses are valid.

rejected.description: Representative responses it rejects. A rubric with no rejected example has not been tested against anything.

task.description: Schema 0.2.0: the concrete reconstruction task the learner performs (a body, givens, numbers or a situation). `produces` says what the attempt should contain; `task` is what the learner is asked to do. Rendered as the Core1B attempt.

representation_ref.description: The representation of this task's own situation (its bodies and values), shown with the Core1B attempt. When absent, Core1B falls back to the first construction unit's (Core1A) figure, which depicts a different situation.

stage_refs.description: Stages of representation_ref safe to show before the attempt; default is the first stage only.

reconstruct.description: The correct construction reached the way a learner would reach it. Held as questions rather than statements: teaching_path is the expert's summary, and a reconstruct route made of statements is that summary under a different key, which is exactly how this product became the declarative one.

route.description: The sequence of asks. Order is meaning: each one is answerable only once the previous has been answered.

ask.description: A question that moves the learner one decision forward. A sentence with a question mark on it is not an ask; the learner must be able to get it wrong.

why_this_ask.description: Why this question rather than another at this point. An author who cannot say this has ordered the route by the expert's convenience.

from_step_ref.description: The teaching_path step this ask arrives at, where one exists. Absent means the learner's route genuinely departs from the expert's, which is why both are held.

differs_from_teaching_path.description: How the learner's route differs from the expert's construction. This is the sentence a reviewer checks the A/B claim against, so it may not restate the teaching path it claims to differ from.

prompt.description: A limiting case, reversal or edge condition.

confirms.description: What passing it establishes, stated so that a recall question cannot be passed off as a boundary test.

answer.description: What passing it looks like. The shared closure invariant has no exception for the last prompt in a cycle.

compact_anchor.description: Schema 0.2.0: the Core1 compact anchor, a one-line instance of the governing relation that makes the map usable before Core1A.

representation_ref.description: The representation of this compact anchor's own situation, shown on the Core1 map. When absent, Core1 falls back to the microtopic's first representation_refs entry, which is often shared across microtopics.

extensions.description: Namespaced subject extensions; no scientific authority is inferred.

mathml.description: Restricted presentation MathML for this relation, so a product can render it without re-authoring.

gate_relation_ref.description: The engineering gate relation this is a bound copy of. Subject truth is owned by the gate registry; the library holds a copy so the compiler can reach it, and that copy is checked against the owner. null says no gate backs this relation: that is true of a subject that declares no gates (a sandbox, or a contract-only subject), and for a subject that has gates Shared/library/authority.py reports it as GATE_RELATION_BINDING_ABSENT.

extensions.description: Namespaced subject extensions; no scientific authority is inferred.

scene_instances.description: Concrete figures satisfying this representation. Everything above states what a figure of this kind must show; an instance states one actual figure, bound to the data it draws, so the library can compile a figure instead of only requiring one.

element.description: The part of the picture, named as required_elements names it.

symbol.description: The symbol it stands for, as the governing relation writes it.

in_words.description: The same thing said in words, which is the third leg of the bridge.

correspondence.description: The representation bridge. required_elements says what the picture must contain and the relation's symbols say what the algebra means, but nothing bound one to the other, so the correspondence a learner must make was asserted rather than held. Naming all three legs is what makes it explicit in both directions rather than a caption pointing one way.

interactive_resource_refs.description: ACTIVITY resources that implement or manipulate this canonical representation. The representation remains academic authority.

reveal_stages.description: Ordered author-defined reveal states for progressive visual support. No global stage count is imposed.

support_stage_map.description: Optional mapping from matrix pre-attempt support level to initial representation stage.

cores.description: Which learner products this figure appears in.

microtopic_ref.description: The microtopic this figure carries. Its obligation is what the compiled figure block is bound to, so a figure can never float free of the teaching it serves.

datum_refs.description: The data records this figure draws. A renderer may only draw values named here.

scene.description: The scene passed to the subject's renderer. Beyond kind, frame and caption the engine enumerates nothing: a renderer declares its own requirements, and a schema that listed them here would have to be edited for every new representation.

asset_ref.description: Authored SVG for this bound scene instance. Optional for legacy topic assets; source snapshots retain their custody path.

question_ref.description: The question this scene is bound to, where it illustrates a question rather than a microtopic. Exactly one of microtopic_ref and question_ref carries the binding; a figure bound to neither is the decoration the role specs refuse.

extensions.description: Namespaced subject extensions; no scientific authority is inferred.

context_refs.description: References application_context records. These classify the scenario/application only and do not add prerequisite or mastery semantics.

extensions.description: Namespaced subject extensions; no scientific authority is inferred.

verification.description: Optional. Names a subject validator family and binds its inputs to datum ids. Absence means no oracle exists, not that the answer is wrong. Additional keys are subject-declared preconditions, passed through to the validator unchanged.

text.description: The hint as the learner reads it.

reveals.description: How far this hint goes. Declared rather than inferred, so that a hint handing over the answer is detectable: an ANSWER hint before the last position defeats the question it is attached to, and for a transfer task a hint revealing the model choice defeats the task itself.

visual_ref.description: Optional canonical representation used by this hint.

visual_stage_ref.description: Optional reveal-stage id within visual_ref; controls how much of canonical visual truth is shown after difficulty.

hints.description: The ladder of source/question hints, in order. Order is meaning here -- Core2 preserves source ordering and custody. Authored Core2/Core2A/Core2B pedagogy belongs in scaffolds[] so source support and authored support are not conflated.

scaffolds.description: Optional authored Core2/Core2A/Core2B pedagogical support, separate from source/question hints[]. Core2 Prompt/Reveal metadata may use prompt + learner_stage; Core2B help must preserve the transfer-protected decision.

transfer.description: The changed demand this task assesses, relative to prior exposure. A task with no transfer block is same-family practice, which is honest; a cover story declared as transfer is what the exposure audit exists to dispute.

dimension.description: Which dimension of demand changes. These are question_family.demand_dimensions' own keys: the family says how much each dimension demands, and this says which one this task moves, in the same words. A cover story is not a dimension, and an enum is what makes that refusable rather than arguable.

statement.description: The changed demand, stated explicitly, so a reviewer can check the transfer claim rather than take the label.

builds_on.description: Exposure lineage: the question or microtopic ids the learner has already seen that this builds on. A transfer claim with no lineage is a claim about a learner nobody has described.

protected_move_ref.description: Stable reasoning-move id for the changed learner decision that pre-attempt help must not hand over.

invariant.description: Schema 0.2.0: what stays valid from the prior exposure (builds_on) while `statement` changes; the learner-facing lineage_continuity_check pairs the two.

novelty.description: Schema 0.2.0: the author's check that this transfer is not a restatement of something the learner has already seen answered (a Core1A worked anchor or diagnose/repair, a Core1B boundary test, a Core2A item). The verifier confirms it.

repair_ref.description: The teaching_path step or misconception this task's predictable failure routes back to. A repair route that points at a whole microtopic is a reading assignment; the spec asks for the specific construction that addresses the failure.

context_refs.description: References application_context records. These classify the scenario/application only and do not add prerequisite or mastery semantics.

independent_check.description: Schema 0.2.0: a structured independent check (with its check_type) when answer.check does not already state it. Not copied from answer.check by migration.

failure_signal.description: The observable sign that this item's learner took the tempting wrong route.

learner_question_type.description: Canonical learner response/question type. Values are governed by Shared/vocabularies/learner-question-metadata.v1.json and must be authored, never inferred from role, stem wording or option shape.

difficulty.description: Canonical authored-question difficulty using the same D1-D4 component model as the competitive-exam bank. Optional at schema level for migration; selected learner products fail closed when it is required and absent.

extensions.description: Namespaced subject extensions; no scientific authority is inferred.

support_posture.description: How much scaffolding this profile standing-instructs. Not the same as practice_control.purpose, which is what a run is for; the two shared the name `purpose`, used different vocabularies, and neither checked the other.

classification.description: SOURCE_CUSTODY_HELD is Core2's hold: the bucket has no frozen or authorised question corpus, next_action names what acquisition would close it, and affected_refs names the bucket. It is a classification rather than a bucket field because a hold is a claim that must say why it is not backed, which is what known_issues is for.

datum.description: A governed quantitative or symbolic value a product may bind to. Without this, the numbers a lesson uses live in a build script and the library cannot drive production. A datum carries its own provenance; it is evidence, not decoration.

extensions.description: Namespaced subject extensions; no scientific authority is inferred.

kind.description: DATUM carries a number with a unit; EQUATION carries a restricted presentation-MathML string.

value.description: A finite number for DATUM, a MathML string for EQUATION.

unit.description: Required for DATUM. A number without a unit is not a governed physical value.

locator.description: Where this value came from: a source location, or an explicit author-created marker.

evidence_of.description: The understanding that criterion is evidence of, so a rubric line cannot be a restatement of the task.

extensions.description: Namespaced subject extensions; no scientific authority is inferred.

visual_stage.description: One author-defined reveal state of a canonical representation. Array order is escalation order; ids are addressable so hints and support mappings can reference stages without copying visual truth.

support_stage_binding.description: Maps one matrix starting-support level to the representation stage visible before the learner attempts. This remains separate from post-failure hint depth.

construction_unit.description: One distinct decision/event of a microtopic's construction, taught as its own unit (Core1A) and reconstructed in Core1B.

decision.description: The move the learner must make in this unit, in words.

step_refs.description: teaching_path step ids this unit covers, in order.

reveal_stage_refs.description: That representation's reveal stages used by this unit, in order.

worked_anchor_ref.description: Question (exposure CORE1A) whose route exercises this unit's move.

bank_anchor_ref.description: A question of the product's bank (an owner-supplied or exam question, not a question of this package) that this unit works through as its worked example: the page shows the question as its owner wrote it with its verified route. Resolved when the product is built, so a package does not carry a copy of the question. Use it for the question the unit builds toward; use worked_anchor_ref for a question the package authors itself.

crux_question_refs.description: Bank questions whose crux this unit builds: the move a learner is most likely to miss in each. The unit is shown as building toward them, takes the reference depth of the hardest of them, and the toughest question of a set must be named here by a unit of the concept it belongs to.

crux_step_ref.description: The teaching_path step of this unit (one of its step_refs) that builds the move named questions in crux_question_refs turn on. The page marks that step, so a reader can see where the unit does the work the hard question needs.

misconception_indexes.description: Indexes into microtopic.misconceptions (wrong path, diagnose, repair).

relation_refs.description: The microtopic's relations this unit uses, shown as the unit's own equation card. Absent: the first unit shows all of the microtopic's relations.

migrated_from.description: Set by package_migrate.py when the unit was derived mechanically (e.g. 'teaching_path'); cleared when an author reviews it.

decision_from.description: Set instead of `decision` when the unit's decision is the microtopic's own field (migration); one source of truth, no copied text.

role.description: The job this item does in a construction unit's 1-2-3 quick check: CHECK recalls the idea, APPLY uses it on a small case, CONNECT says which idea it leads to next.

purpose.description: What the rung does for the learner; a ladder climbs from ORIENT to FIRST_RELATION before any ANSWER.

from.description: The legacy hint or scaffold this rung is; its text is read from there (no copied text).

initial_ref.description: Shown with the stem, before any attempt (Core2A initial_representation).

safe_ref.description: Shown before commitment; must not show the protected move (Core2B).

bound_ref.description: Shown with support or the solution (may show the move).

closure.description: What this item establishes for the family, which a later transfer (Core2B) builds on.

band.description: Derived D-band. Must match the component sum through Shared/vocabularies/learner-question-metadata.v1.json; consumers must not treat an intended cohort as authority for this field.

requested_band.description: Optional planning/stress-cohort target. It may differ from band and is never used to select the QRT cell.

component_evidence.description: Optional question-specific evidence for the five authored 0–2 difficulty components. When present, every component must be justified against Shared/vocabularies/learner-question-metadata.v1.json question_difficulty_component_rubric. Omission preserves legacy records; acceptance policy may require it for newly adjudicated classifications.

availability.description: Optional disclosure boundary for this authored completion. PRE_ATTEMPT_SAFE is allowed before commitment, AFTER_ATTEMPT becomes available after a valid learner commitment without revealing the full solution, and POST_SOLUTION stays inside the solution disclosure. Omission preserves legacy behavior.

Optional disclosure boundary for this authored completion. PRE_ATTEMPT_SAFE is allowed before commitment, AFTER_ATTEMPT becomes available after a valid learner commitment without revealing the full solution, and POST_SOLUTION stays inside the solution disclosure. Omission preserves legacy behavior.

core2_support_plan.description: Opt-in links to existing question reasoning moves, support rows and bound visual stages. Availability may distinguish pre-attempt-safe, after-attempt support, and solution-only disclosure. Omitted availability preserves legacy behavior: support completing protected work remains solution-only. Unlisted support retains its existing reveal semantics; authors must record completion honestly.
